title: Minimum Bishop Moves to Reach Target
summary: Given an 8x8 chessboard with 1-indexed rows and columns, a bishop starts at a specified position and aims to reach a target position.
statement: Given an 8x8 chessboard with 1-indexed rows and columns, a bishop starts at a specified position and aims to reach a target position. The bishop can move along any diagonal direction within the board. Determine the minimum number of moves required for the bishop to reach the target position, or return -1 if it is impossible to reach the target.
constraints: source and target are distinct cells on an 8 by 8 board.
A bishop moves any positive distance along a diagonal.
Return the minimum moves, or -1 when the target is unreachable.
reference_solution:
def minimum_bishop_moves(source,target):
    if sum(source)%2!=sum(target)%2:return -1
    if abs(source[0]-target[0])==abs(source[1]-target[1]):return 1
    return 2

hints: A bishop never changes square color, so opposite colors are unreachable.
On the same diagonal, absolute row and column differences match and one move suffices.
Any two same-colored cells not sharing a diagonal meet through an intermediate diagonal in two moves.
These mutually exclusive cases give the exact minimum.
editorial: These mutually exclusive cases give the exact minimum.
